items.narrative:
This audit covers 47 supply-chain events recorded between 2025-02-05 and 2025-06-15, spanning 7 critical tracking event types—cooling, first land-based receiving, harvesting, initial packing, receiving, shipping, and transformation—across 6 external trading partners and 14 products. Of those 14 products, 5 are definitively on the Food Traceability List, 6 are classified as suspicious (meaning their traceability obligations remain unresolved), and only 3 are confirmed off-list. Shipping dominates the event record with 19 of the 47 events, while cooling and first land-based receiving each account for only 3.

The most severe problems, in order of urgency, are as follows. Nine findings are rated high severity and 33 medium, for a total of 42 findings across the audit. The single largest finding category is scope or exemption uncertainty, which generated 8 findings—meaning the business cannot currently confirm which of its products are legally subject to traceability requirements. Compounding this, 4 products carry declared FTL classifications that conflict with the inferred tier: products 10860004520037 and 10860004520099 are declared as General grocery yet are assessed as definite_on the list, and products 10860004520020 and 10860004520113 are declared General grocery yet flagged as suspicious. Inbound ERP mismatches produced 5 findings, KDE completeness gaps account for 4 findings with 21 key data elements missing out of 441 graded, and lot integrity issues collectively generated 11 findings covering backward lineage gaps (2 gaps, 1 needs-review), date ordering (2 needs-review), duplicate TLC codes (2 needs-review), forward linkage (1 needs-review), mass balance (2 needs-review), and a self-receive anomaly (1 needs-review). Two trading partners—Metro Grocers Inc and Sunbelt Restaurants Group—are both rated band D, the lowest compliance band, despite accounting for 11 and 8 events respectively.

The immediate next steps are: first, convene a product classification review for all 6 suspicious-tier products and the 4 declared-vs-inferred mismatches, prioritizing 10860004520037 and 10860004520099 which are already assessed as definite_on; second, issue corrective data requests to Metro Grocers Inc and Sunbelt Restaurants Group, both band D partners, requiring them to remediate the data quality issues behind their low band ratings before the next event cycle; third, investigate and close the 5 inbound ERP mismatch findings and the 21 missing KDEs, as these directly undermine the 0.9524 KDE coverage rate and will worsen under regulatory scrutiny; and fourth, resolve the 2 backward lineage gaps and the remaining lot integrity needs-review items to establish a clean, auditable lot chain across all 13 linked lots.
